from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex signals are sums of simple sine waves.",
            "See the waveform break into individual clean waves.",
            "Nature's rhythm is built from simple periodic parts."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Symphony of Waves", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define the complex wave and its components
        x_range = [0, 4 * PI]
        complex_func = lambda x: np.sin(x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x) + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * x)
        wave_complex = FunctionGraph(complex_func, x_range=x_range, color=WHITE)
        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=x_range, color=BLUE)
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=x_range, color=GREEN)
        wave3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(5 * x), x_range=x_range, color=RED)
        
        waves = VGroup(wave1, wave2, wave3)
        self.place_in_area(wave_complex, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(wave_complex))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Explode into parts
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(wave_complex.copy(), wave1),
            ReplacementTransform(wave_complex.copy(), wave2),
            ReplacementTransform(wave_complex.copy(), wave3),
            wave_complex.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(waves),
            wave_complex.animate.set_stroke(opacity=1.0)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier series decomposes signals into harmonic components.",
            "Coefficients determine the weight of each component.",
            "Watch the square wave form, piece by piece.",
            "Harmonics build the signal's unique profile.",
            "Integration reveals the amplitude of every frequency."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Framework: The Harmonic Foundation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula setup
        formula = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left( a_n \cos\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) + b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) \right)",
            font_size=30
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3")
        
        # Discrete components setup
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(5)])
        for i, dot in enumerate(points):
            self.place_at_grid(dot, f"D{i+1}")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Highlight coefficients in formula (approximate indices)
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][6:8]), Indicate(formula[0][17:19])) 

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(points.animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color("#FFA500"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: The Epicycles Construction", [
            "Rotating vectors trace complex paths easily.",
            "Epicycles add layers to create shapes.",
            "Observe the Fourier robot drawing patterns.",
            "Circles define the rhythm of the motion.",
            "Geometry turns abstract math into clear visualization."
        ])

        # Setup epicycles
        center = self.grid["C3"]
        v1 = Vector([2, 0], color="#FF00FF").shift(center)
        v2 = Vector([1, 0], color="#FFFF00").shift(v1.get_end())
        
        circle1 = Circle(radius=2, color="#FF00FF", stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(center)
        circle2 = Circle(radius=1, color="#FFFF00", stroke_opacity=0.3).move_to(v1.get_end())

        path = TracedPath(v2.get_end, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), Create(circle1), GrowArrow(v1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(circle2), GrowArrow(v2))
        self.add(path)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Animate rotation
        v1_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        v2_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        v1.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(v1_tracker.get_value()).shift(center - m.get_start()))
        v2.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(v2_tracker.get_value()).shift(v1.get_end() - m.get_start()))
        circle2.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(v1.get_end()))
        
        self.play(v1_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), v2_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Why it Matters", [
            "Fourier transforms are essential for noise cancellation.",
            "Compression algorithms use frequencies to store images.",
            "Technology relies on splitting signals into components."
        ])
        
        # Create signals
        # Original noisy signal: sum of low + high frequency
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        
        noisy_func = lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(10 * np.pi * x)
        clean_func = lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * x)
        
        noisy_graph = axes.plot(noisy_func, color=RED)
        clean_graph = axes.plot(clean_func, color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(noisy_graph)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Transform(noisy_graph, clean_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Highlight signals by showing them apart
        separated = VGroup(
            axes.copy(),
            axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(10 * np.pi * x), color=RED).scale(0.8)
        ).arrange(DOWN).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(separated, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(separated))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [

            "Time and frequency domains represent signal data.",
            "Analyze complex patterns by splitting them apart."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        prism_text = Text("Frequency Prism", color="#FFFF00")
        formula = MathTex(r"f(t) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} c_n e^{in\omega t}")
        overview = VGroup(
            Text("Time Domain", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.7),
            Text("Frequency Domain", color="#FF00FF").scale(0.7)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(prism_text, "B3")
        self.play(Write(prism_text), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_in_area(overview, "E1", "F6")
        self.play(FadeIn(overview), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Rhythm of Signals

sections.title: The Hook: The Symphony of Waves
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex periodic signal (like a cat's purr or a violin note) can be broken down into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of sine/cosine functions and superposition.
sections.example: Visualizing a complex waveform on an oscilloscope suddenly 'exploding' into several individual, clean sine waves of different frequencies.

sections.title: Mathematical Framework: The Harmonic Foundation
sections.content: Define the Fourier Series formula for a function f(x) with period T. Focus on the intuition behind a0, an, and bn. Use visuals showing how these coefficients determine the 'weight' or 'volume' of each individual sine component.
sections.example: An animation of a 3D bar chart where each bar represents an amplitude coefficient (an/bn), constructing a square wave piece by piece.

sections.title: Visualization: The Epicycles Construction
sections.content: Explain how adding rotating vectors (phasors) reconstructs a shape. This makes the abstract coefficients intuitive by mapping them to geometric rotations.
sections.example: An animated 'Fourier Robot' drawing a character's face (like a famous cartoon rabbit) by drawing circles upon circles.

sections.title: Application: Why it Matters
sections.content: Connect the math to real-world technology: noise cancellation in headphones, image compression (JPEG), and voice recognition.
sections.example: A 'Noise-Cancelling Owl' headset diagram: the device detects an incoming 'noisy' wave and plays the exact inverse Fourier components to create silence.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Fourier series is the 'prism' that splits complex signals into a 'rainbow' of frequencies. Reiterate that the series is a tool to move between Time Domain and Frequency Domain.
sections.example: A split-screen graphic: On the left, a wiggly time-domain signal; on the right, a static frequency-domain 'spectrum' that makes the data easy to analyze.
